references.text: Aaron and his sons shall be anointed and consecrated to the priestly service, with the same command to anoint and sanctify them as priests.
Describes the actual anointing ritual where the anointing oil is poured over Aaron's head.
Aaron and his sons are consecrated to the priestly service as a permanent ordinance.
Repetition of the command to anoint Aaron and his sons for the priestly service.
The fulfillment of the command where Moses anoints Aaron with the holy oil.
Moses anoints Aaron and his sons along with their garments to consecrate them.
Refers to Aaron's sons who were anointed and consecrated to the priestly service.
Poetic description of the anointing oil running down over Aaron's head and beard.
Describes how every high priest is taken from among men and appointed for service to God.
Contrasts the Levitical priesthood with Christ as the perfect high priest consecrated by oath.
Describes the actual execution of the consecration for Aaron as the head, which forms the basis for the entire priestly line.
Links the sanctification of the tent of meeting with the sanctification of the priests as a unified act.
Emphasizes the necessity of proper consecration by showing the death penalty for those not holy to the service.
Confirms that the entire seven-day ceremony is necessary to complete the consecration mentioned in 30:30.
